newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat condemns Tel Aviv bomb, rejects accusations.
newsitem.headline: Arafat condemns Tel Aviv bomb, rejects accusations.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat condemned a blast that killed three people at a Tel Aviv cafe on Friday and his spokesman angrily rejected Israeli charges that Arafat bore indirect responsiblity for the attack.
Spokesman Marwan Kanafani called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a liar for accusing Arafat and placed responsibility for the bloodshed on the Israeli leader.
Kanafani told Reuters that Arafat called Israel's President Ezer Weizman and said: "I am very disturbed with the violence that took place today and I condemn this terrorist incident".
The blast killed three people, including the suspected Moslem suicide bomber, and wounded 43, police said.

Israeli security officials had warned that violence by Palestinians, including possible suicide attacks, could erupt this week in reprisal for Netanyahu's groundbreaking for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
An anonymous caller to police said the Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas was responsible for the attack.

Netanyahu reiterated after the attack his contention that Arafat's Palestinian Authority gave a green light to "terrorist organisations" to resume attacks like suicide bombings that killed 59 Israelis a year ago.

"Arafat has not given anyone the green light to use violence, on the contrary he called for non-violence," said Mahmoud Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, who led PLO's negotiations with Israel leading to a 1993 interim peace accord.
"Our policy has always been and continues to be the rejection of using terrorism and violence in solving problems," he told Reuters.
Abu Mazen said the PLO would stick to a policy of solving problems through peaceful means.
"It's a shame that the Israeli prime minister lies in front of his people and holds President Arafat responsible," Kanafani said.

"The person ultimately responsible for this painful deed is Netanyahu himself who did not listen to the advice of the international community and he led us all to this position and to this hopeless atmosphere that resulted in the loss of lives of some innocent people."
Israel came under intense international criticism for its settlement project that Palestinians said violated Israel-PLO peace accords that leave the status of Jerusalem open for future negotiations.
Arafat's spokesman appealed for a renewal of peace contacts.

"Prime Minister Netanyahu should carry the responsibility bravely and should put his hand in the hand of President Arafat to find a solution to this crisis instead of advancing accusations that will not lead to any solution," Kanafani said.
Arafat's Palestinian police force in the Gaza Strip prevented busloads of Hamas supporters from reaching the town of Khan Yunis where they were to attend a rally against Israel's settlement policy.
Ibrahim al-Makadmeh, a Hamas leader freed by the Palestinian Authority last week, told the rally that only bombs could stop Israel from building the new settlement in East Jerusalem.

"We must have the control and the power to stop the bulldozers of the enemy -- and our unarmed people will not prevent it but the holy warriors carrying explosives on their shoulders and exploding the enemies of God," he said.
